annual: Priced the annual tier at $290 a year, assuming 4% monthly churn.
costs: Finished the cost analysis on the engine this week, using the last month of real traffic rather than estimates. Most batches only ever cost one model call, because the contribution gate stops them before the scout runs. A full pass through all four stages comes to about 2.3 cents; the median batch is closer to 1.3. Averaged across the test accounts that works out to roughly $4.25 per seat per month for a normally active team. Heavier channels push it higher, but nothing I've seen goes past about $7. team. leads: Wrapped up the pricing conversations I've been having with team leads. Three so far: one at a twelve-person agency, one running engineering at a mid-size SaaS company, and one leading a university research group. All three assumed per-seat pricing without me raising it. When I asked where the approval line sat, two named $15 a seat as the point where they'd have to involve finance, and the third said anything under $10 he could expense without asking anyone. None of them pushed back on paying monthly.
testers: Ran the numbers on the engine this week: it stays quiet on roughly 90% of batches. That's the design doing its job. Talked to three testers. Two of them said they weren't sure the bot was even running, because they hadn't seen it post anything.
onboarding: Shipped the onboarding rewrite last sprint — nine screens down to four, with account setup and workspace creation collapsed into a single page instead of three. Completion went from 41% to 68% over the two weeks since it went out, measured across everyone who started signup. The drop-off that used to happen on the old screen five is essentially gone.
tickets: Finished going through last quarter's support tickets, all 22 of them. Fourteen were people stuck partway through setup, and most of those never got as far as creating a workspace. The remainder split between billing questions and a single integration bug.
load: Finished load testing the Teams integration against a simulated company. One deployment kept up with 40 teams posting at the same time, and every card still landed within 25 seconds of the message that triggered it. Nothing queued up or got dropped, even at the peak.
wave: Heard back from everyone we invited to test. In total, 12 companies said yes, and 8 of them asked to bring more than one team, so the first wave is closer to 30 teams than 12. A couple of them would like to start in the same week.
